label: Enacted rate
methodology: Members are ranked within their own chamber — the House and the Senate are ranked separately, because their vote counts and calendars differ. For each metric a member's rank is their position when members are ordered by that metric's value, highest first, using standard competition ranking: members with the same value share a rank, and the next rank skips accordingly. A member's percentile is the percentage of the ranked members in their chamber whose value is lower than theirs, so the count behind every percentile is visible. The chamber mean and median, and the mean for each party (grouped by the member's current party), are published alongside. A rank is a position in an ordering, not a judgment; this layer attaches no label to it. Members with no value for a metric (for example, no enacted rate when they sponsored no bills) are not ranked on that metric. Non-voting House delegates are ranked only on bills sponsored, bills cosponsored, and enacted rate; they are left out of the attendance and party-unity rankings because they cannot vote on final passage, so those figures are measured over a different, smaller set of votes and are not comparable to a voting member's.
